AI Statement and Descriptive Log¶

AI Statement¶

This project has used the free VS Code Copilot generative AI to: Generate code, identify bugs, fix bugs, brainstorm technical solutions, and to teach the process of coding through in-depth explanations of each generated line of code. Some Google searches have also involved Google's built-in generative AI.

The project author has steered the AI's coding through accepting, rejecting, and modifying the AI's code based on the author's intuition. The author has requested code explanations, studied the AI's code, and made explanatory comments for each code block based on the author's understanding.

The code provided is therefore created partly by the author and partly by generative AI. The explanatory code comments are written exclusively by the author.

1.1 Connecting to Cassandra¶

In [ ]:
# This code is copied from D2DBook from khliland's IND320 GitHub Repo.
# Because the connection and testing of connection is simple, the author
# has not modified it outside of path directories, logins, etc.

# Connecting to Cassandra
from cassandra.cluster import Cluster
cluster = Cluster(['localhost'], port=9042)
session = cluster.connect()

# Set up new keyspace (first time only)
#                                              name of keyspace                        replication strategy           replication factor
session.execute("CREATE KEYSPACE IF NOT EXISTS my_first_keyspace WITH REPLICATION = { 'class' : 'SimpleStrategy', 'replication_factor' : 1 };")

# Create a new table (first time only)
session.set_keyspace('my_first_keyspace')
session.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS my_first_keyspace.my_first_table;") # Starting from scratch every time
session.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS my_first_table (ind int PRIMARY KEY, company text, model text);")

# Insert some data (ind is the primary key, must be unique)
session.execute("INSERT INTO my_first_table (ind, company, model) VALUES (1, 'Tesla', 'Model Y');")
session.execute("INSERT INTO my_first_table (ind, company, model) VALUES (2, 'Tesla', 'Model 3');")
session.execute("INSERT INTO my_first_table (ind, company, model) VALUES (3, 'Polestar', '3');")

# Query the data
rows = session.execute("SELECT * FROM my_first_table;")
for i in rows:
    print(i)

3. ENTSO-E API¶

3.1 Initial Setup; API Key, BRZ Pairings, Defining Start/End¶

In [ ]:
from entsoe import EntsoePandasClient

# Setting up ENTSO-E API client w/ previously obtained security token.
api_key = open("../No Sync/ENTSO-E_API.txt").read()
client = EntsoePandasClient(api_key=api_key)

# Finding BRZ pairings to get total in/out Norway (used map on Transparency
# Platform website to find pairings).
brz_pairings = {
    "NO_1": ["SE_3"],
    "NO_2": ["DK_1", "GB", "DE_LU", "NL"],
    "NO_3": ["SE_2"],
    "NO_4": ["SE_1", "SE_2", "FI", "RU"],
}

# Selecting start and end points for data collection as ordered by task.
end = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC").floor("h")
start = end - pd.DateOffset(years=2)

3.2 AI-Derived Abomination (Collecting Relevant API Data)¶

In [ ]:
# This takes 15-40 minutes to produce its full output, depends on API.
# The core function in this cell is .query_crossborder_flows(). This
# retrieves relevant data from the ENTSO-E API. In order to avoid
# manually inputing the different parameters to filter for each type of
# data relevancy (BRZ, in/out, time period), AI was utilised to create an
# iterating process. The AI proposal has been simplified substantially,
# but the code is still bulky.

from entsoe.exceptions import NoMatchingDataError

flow_results = {}
flow_frames = []

# See print in innermost for-loop.
total_requests = sum(len(neighbours) * 2 for neighbours in brz_pairings.values())
request_number = 0

# Iterating over each Norwegian zone in brz_pairings (NO1, NO2, etc.) AND
# each associated neighbour. Some Norwegian zones have multiple neighbours,
# hence two for-loops for this step.
for norway_zone, neighbours in brz_pairings.items():
    for neighbour_zone in neighbours:
        
        # Defining flow direction variables.
        directions = [
            ("out", norway_zone, neighbour_zone),
            ("in", neighbour_zone, norway_zone),
        ]

        # Iterating over each direction.
        for direction, from_zone, to_zone in directions:
            request_number += 1

            # Printing progress (looong wait times).
            print(
                f"[{request_number}/{total_requests}] "
                f"Requesting {direction}: {from_zone} -> {to_zone}"
            )

            # Getting relevant data from ENTSO-E API. "Relevant" data is
            # data that fits within the defined start and end points, and
            # corresponds to the selected zone pairing in brz_pairings.
            try:
                series = client.query_crossborder_flows(
                    from_zone,
                    to_zone,
                    start=start,
                    end=end,
                )
            except NoMatchingDataError:
                print(f"No data returned for {from_zone} -> {to_zone}")
                continue

            # Keep the Series keyed by the Norway zone, neighbour, and direction.
            flow_results[(norway_zone, neighbour_zone, direction)] = series

            # Also add it to a single table for later Spark/Cassandra work.
            part = series.rename("flow_mw").rename_axis("timestamp").reset_index()
            part["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(part["timestamp"], utc=True)
            part["norway_zone"] = norway_zone
            part["neighbor_zone"] = neighbour_zone
            part["direction"] = direction
            flow_frames.append(part)

if not flow_frames:
    raise RuntimeError("No flow data was returned for any of the requested borders.")

flows_df = pd.concat(flow_frames, ignore_index=True)

print(f"Collected {len(flows_df):,} observations.")

3.3.3 CSV Workaround (See Log): Writing Backup CSV to Cassandra¶

In [ ]:
# AI magic.
import time
import pandas as pd
from cassandra.concurrent import execute_concurrent_with_args

csv_path = "retrieved_api_data.csv"

# The csv includes 1million+ rows. Splitting into chunks for efficiency.
chunk_size = 100_000
concurrency = 100

# Preparing Cassandra table. Realized mixed spelling of "neighbor" too late.
insert = session.prepare("""
    INSERT INTO my_first_keyspace.crossborder_flows
        (norway_zone, neighbor_zone, direction, timestamp, flow_mw)
    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
""")

start = time.perf_counter()
rows_processed = 0
rows_failed = 0

# Iterating over each chunk in csv, chunk size already set.
for chunk_number, chunk in enumerate(
    pd.read_csv(csv_path, chunksize=chunk_size, parse_dates=["timestamp"]),
    start=1,
):
    # Selecting tuple values.
    parameters = (
        (
            row.norway_zone,
            row.neighbor_zone,
            row.direction,
            pd.Timestamp(row.timestamp).to_pydatetime(),
            float(row.flow_mw),
        )
        for row in chunk.itertuples(index=False)
    )

    results = execute_concurrent_with_args(
        session,
        insert,
        parameters,
        concurrency=concurrency,
        raise_on_first_error=False,
    )

    failed_results = [result for result in results if not result[0]]
    rows_processed += len(results)
    rows_failed += len(failed_results)

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    print(
        f"Processed {rows_processed:,} rows "
        f"({rows_failed:,} failed) in {elapsed / 60:.1f} minutes"
    )

    # Show a few errors so failures aren't hidden.
    for _, error in failed_results[:3]:
        print("Insert error:", error)

if rows_failed:
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Finished processing, but {rows_failed:,} of {rows_processed:,} inserts failed."
    )

print(f"All {rows_processed:,} rows inserted in "
      f"{(time.perf_counter() - start) / 60:.1f} minutes.")

# Making copy of pandas API df for plotting.
data_pie = retrieved_api_data.copy()

# Converting API data columns to pandas datetime and numberic objects.
data_pie["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(data_pie["timestamp"], utc=True)
data_pie["flow_mw"] = pd.to_numeric(data_pie["flow_mw"])

# Selecting zones for plotting.
zones_pie = ["NO_4", "SE_1"]



# Defining time period for plotting (one year).
latest_timestamp = data_pie["timestamp"].max()
one_year_ago = latest_timestamp - pd.DateOffset(years=1)

# Selecting data for defined time period and zones.
plot_data_pie = data_pie.loc[data_pie["timestamp"] >= one_year_ago]
plot_data_pie = plot_data_pie.loc[
    (plot_data_pie["norway_zone"] == zones_pie[0]) &
    (plot_data_pie["neighbor_zone"] == zones_pie[1])]



# Summing incoming and outgoing MW flows for each zone.
zone_totals_pie = (
    plot_data_pie.groupby("direction")["flow_mw"]
    .sum()
    .reindex(["in", "out"], fill_value=0))



# Plotting.
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.pie(
    zone_totals_pie,
    labels=["Flow in (SE_1 → NO_4)", "Flow out (NO_4 → SE_1)"],
    autopct="%1.1f%%",
    startangle=90,
)
plt.title("Flow in and out on the NO_4–SE_1 connection — most recent year")
plt.axis("equal")
plt.show()

3.8 Insert ENTSO-E API data into MongoDB¶

In [ ]:
# MongoDB client is already defined in 1.3.
collection = client["ENTSO-E_MW_Flow"]["data"]

batch_size = 100_000
inserted = 0

for frame in pd.read_csv(csv_path, chunksize=batch_size):
    # Convert pandas missing values to Python None, which MongoDB stores as null.
    frame = frame.astype(object).where(pd.notna(frame), None)
    documents = frame.to_dict(orient="records")

    if documents:
        result = collection.insert_many(documents, ordered=False)
        inserted += len(result.inserted_ids)

print(f"Inserted {inserted:,} documents.")
print(f"Collection now contains {collection.count_documents({}):,} documents.")

# reloaded with every Streamlit page action.
@st.cache_data
def load_data():
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

    # Translating Norwegian column names into understandable English.
    df = df.rename(columns={
        "dato_Id": "Date",
        "omrType": "Area Type",
        "omrnr": "Area Number",
        "iso_aar": "ISO Year",
        "iso_uke": "ISO Week",
        "fyllingsgrad": "Filling Ratio",
        "kapasitet_TWh": "Capacity TWh",
        "fylling_TWh": "Filling TWh",
        "neste_Publiseringsdato": "Next Publishing Date",
        "fyllingsgrad_forrige_uke": "FR Last Week",
        "endring_fyllingsgrad": "Change FR",
    })

    # Sorting by date, oldest to newest.
    df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    return df.sort_values("Date", ascending=True)

# Instructing Streamlit to cache load data function so the data isn't
# reloaded with every Streamlit page action.
@st.cache_data
def load_data(url="https://biapi.nve.no/magasinstatistikk/api/Magasinstatistikk/HentOffentligData"):
    
    # Retrieving data from API with .get().
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    
    df = pd.DataFrame(response.json())

    # Translating Norwegian column names into understandable English.
    df = df.rename(columns={
        "dato_Id": "Date",
        "omrType": "Area Type",
        "omrnr": "Area Number",
        "iso_aar": "ISO Year",
        "iso_uke": "ISO Week",
        "fyllingsgrad": "Filling Ratio",
        "kapasitet_TWh": "Capacity TWh",
        "fylling_TWh": "Filling TWh",
        "neste_Publiseringsdato": "Next Publishing Date",
        "fyllingsgrad_forrige_uke": "FR Last Week",
        "endring_fyllingsgrad": "Change FR",
    })

    # Sorting by date, oldest to newest.
    df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    return df.sort_values("Date", ascending=True)

In [ ]:
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from pymongo import MongoClient
from pymongo.server_api import ServerApi

# Instructing Streamlit to cache load data function so the csv isn't
# reloaded with every Streamlit page action.
@st.cache_data

# Defining function to load MongoDB data into pandas df.
def load_flow_data() -> pd.DataFrame:
    
    # Using Path to set path relative to module directory. Default is
    # Streamlit working directory, which is not necessarily reliable.
    psw_file = (
        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "No Sync" / "MongoDB.txt")
    
    psw = psw_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

    uri = ("mongodb+srv://ipynb_user:"+psw+ "@nylandcluster.zizrxuq.mongodb.net/")

    # Retrieving MongoDB data.
    with MongoClient(uri, server_api=ServerApi("1")) as client:
        collection = client["ENTSO-E_MW_Flow"]["data"]
        documents = list(collection.find({}, {"_id": 0}))

    return pd.DataFrame.from_records(documents)

from modules.api import load_data
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

# Loading API into df.
df = load_data()

# Creating page title and API load information.
st.title("Reservoir data")
st.write(f"Loaded {len(df):,} rows.")



# --- Plotting Setup ---

# Selecting df columns to include in chart. Plotting ISO weeks/years
# is considered unnecessary.
columns_to_plot = [
    "Filling Ratio",
    "Filling TWh",
    "FR Last Week",
    "Change FR",
]

# Taking user input to decide which area type is to be plotted.
plot_area_type = st.radio(
    "Select area type",
    options=["EL", "NO", "VASS"],
)

# Selecting data for the chosen area type. Each area number gets its
# own sparkline column so values from different regions are not mixed.
plot_data = df[df["Area Type"] == plot_area_type]
area_numbers = sorted(plot_data["Area Number"].unique())

# Creating chart title and information.
st.write(
    f"Showing {plot_area_type} areas {', '.join(map(str, area_numbers))} "
    f"from {plot_data['Date'].min().date()} to {plot_data['Date'].max().date()}."
)

# Creating one LineChartColumn per area number.
chart_table = pd.DataFrame({"Data category": columns_to_plot})
column_config = {}
for area_number in area_numbers:
    area_data = plot_data[plot_data["Area Number"] == area_number]
    area_column = f"Area {area_number}"
    chart_table[area_column] = [
        area_data[column].dropna().tolist() for column in columns_to_plot
    ]
    column_config[area_column] = st.column_config.LineChartColumn(area_column)

st.dataframe(
    chart_table,
    column_config=column_config,
    hide_index=True,
    use_container_width=True,
)

from modules.api import load_data
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

# Loading csv into df.
df = load_data()

# Creating page title and csv load information.
st.title("Data Plots")
st.write(f"Select data type and range to plot.")



# --- Plotting Setup ---

# Selecting csv columns to include in chart. Plotting ISO weeks/years
# is considered unnecessary.
columns_to_plot = [
    "Filling Ratio",
    "Filling TWh",
    "FR Last Week",
    "Change FR",
]

# Taking user input to decide which area type is to be plotted.
plot_area_type = st.radio(
    "Select area type",
    options=["EL", "NO", "VASS"])

# Selecting offered area numbers based on user input for area type.
if plot_area_type == "EL":
    area_number_options = list(range(1, 6))
elif plot_area_type == "NO":
    area_number_options = [0]
else:
    area_number_options = list(range(1, 4))

# Taking user input to decide which area number is to be plotted.
plot_area_number = st.selectbox(
    "Select area number",
    options=area_number_options)

# Selecting data from df matching specified area type and number.
# Plotting all data in chart will lead to overlapping dates, as
# multiple area types and numbers share the same dates.
plot_data = df[
    (df["Area Type"] == plot_area_type)
    & (df["Area Number"] == plot_area_number)
    ][["Date", *columns_to_plot]].set_index("Date")



# --- Selection Slider ---

# Preparing selectable months for selection slider using list:
# * plot_data.index selects the index values (Date) for each column
#   in plot_data. These dates are already sorted chronologically.
# * .to_period("M") converts the dates into monthly periods.
# * .unique() makes the months show up only once in the slider.
# * .tolist() makes available_months a Python list. We now have a de-
#    duplicated, ordered list of available months for our slider.
available_months = plot_data.index.to_period("M").unique().tolist()

# Creating selection slider for selecting specific subsets of months,
# using ready-made available_months list.
start_month, end_month = st.select_slider(
    "Select months",
    options=available_months,
    value=(available_months[0], available_months[0]),
    format_func=str,
)

# Creating pandas object for plotting monthly data in figures. Some
# months in the CSV have more observations than others.
plot_months = plot_data.index.to_period("M")

# Selecting months from plot_months based on selection slider input.
selected_data = plot_data.loc[
    (plot_months >= start_month) & (plot_months <= end_month)
]



# --- Selection Box ---

# Creating selection box.
selected_column = st.selectbox(
    "Column to plot",
    options=["All columns", *columns_to_plot],
)

# Selecting column(s) to plot based on selection box input, default
# "All columns".
selected_columns = (
    columns_to_plot if selected_column == "All columns" else [selected_column]
)



# --- Plotting ---

# Creating plot based on selected colum(s) and data.
st.write(
    f"Showing {plot_area_type} area {plot_area_number} "
    f"from {selected_data.index.min().date()} to {selected_data.index.max().date()}."
)
st.subheader("Reservoir metrics over time")
st.line_chart(
    selected_data,
    y=selected_columns,
    x_label="Date",
    y_label="Metric value",
)

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from modules.mongoDBconnection import load_flow_data

st.title("Pie and Line Charts")

df = load_flow_data()

# Converting API data columns to pandas datetime and numberic objects.
df["timestamp"] = pd.to_datetime(df["timestamp"], utc=True)
df["flow_mw"] = pd.to_numeric(df["flow_mw"])

# Splitting page into left and right columns.
left_column, right_column = st.columns(2)

# Creating dictionary of paired zones from ENTSO-E map.
brz_pairings = {
    "NO_1": ["SE_3"],
    "NO_2": ["DK_1", "GB", "DE_LU", "NL"],
    "NO_3": ["SE_2"],
    "NO_4": ["SE_1", "SE_2", "FI", "RU"],
}


# --- LEFT COLUMN ---

with left_column:

    # Pulling connections out of the brz_pairings dictionary.
    connections = [
        f"{norway_zone} ↔ {neighbor_zone}"
        for norway_zone, neighbor_zones in brz_pairings.items()
        for neighbor_zone in neighbor_zones]

    # Creating radio buttons to let user select plotting connection.
    selected_connection = st.radio("Select connection", options=connections)
    zones = selected_connection.split(" ↔ ")
    st.subheader(f"Flow in and out on the {zones[0]}–{zones[1]} connection")

    # Creating selection box to take user input for year.
    selected_year = st.selectbox("Select year", options=[2025, 2026])
    year_data = df[df["timestamp"].dt.year == selected_year]

    # Selecting data based on zones and user-inputted year.
    year_data = year_data[
        (year_data["norway_zone"] == zones[0])
        & (year_data["neighbor_zone"] == zones[1])]
    
    pie_data = (
        year_data.groupby("direction")["flow_mw"]
        .sum()
        .reindex(["in", "out"], fill_value=0)
        .rename_axis("Direction")
        .reset_index(name="Flow (MW)")
        .replace({"Direction": {"in": f"In: {zones[1]} to {zones[0]}", "out": f"Out: {zones[0]} to {zones[1]}"}}))

    # Plotting using built-in Streamlit functions.
    st.vega_lite_chart(
        pie_data,
        {
            "mark": {"type": "arc", "outerRadius": 120},
            "encoding": {
                "theta": {"field": "Flow (MW)", "type": "quantitative"},
                "color": {
                    "field": "Direction",
                    "type": "nominal",
                    "legend": {"orient": "bottom", "direction": "horizontal"},
                },
                "tooltip": [
                    {"field": "Direction", "type": "nominal"},
                    {"field": "Flow (MW)", "type": "quantitative"},
                ],
            },
        },
        use_container_width=True,
    )



# --- RIGHT COLUMN ---

with right_column:
    st.subheader(f"Flow between {zones[0]} and {zones[1]}")

    # Defining time period for data (last year).
    latest_timestamp = df["timestamp"].max()
    one_year_ago = latest_timestamp - pd.DateOffset(years=1)

    # Selecting data for plotting based on time period and connection.
    line_data = df[
        (df["timestamp"] >= one_year_ago)
        & (df["norway_zone"] == zones[0])
        & (df["neighbor_zone"] == zones[1])
    ].sort_values("timestamp")

    # Defining months the user can select.
    if line_data.empty:
        st.info("No data is available for this connection in the most recent year.")
    else:
        months = (
            line_data["timestamp"]
            .dt.strftime("%b %Y")
            .drop_duplicates()
            .tolist()[::-1])

        # Creating pills for selecting months. Default is most recent.
        selected_months = st.pills(
            "Select months",
            options=months,
            default=months[0],
            selection_mode="multi",)

        # Formatting each month as label shown in Streamlit.
        if selected_months:
            plot_data = line_data[
                line_data["timestamp"].dt.strftime("%b %Y").isin(selected_months)]

            # Plotting.
            flow_by_direction = (
                plot_data.pivot_table(
                    index="timestamp",
                    columns="direction",
                    values="flow_mw",
                    aggfunc="sum",
                )
                .rename(
                    columns={
                        "out": f"Out: {zones[0]} to {zones[1]}",
                        "in": f"In: {zones[1]} to {zones[0]}",
                    }
                )
                .sort_index())

            st.line_chart(
                flow_by_direction,
                x_label="Date",
                y_label="Flow (MW)",)
        else:
            st.info("Select one or more months to display the line chart.")



# --- Source information ---

with st.expander("About this data"):
    st.write(
        """
        The charts use ENTSO-E flow data stored in the project's MongoDB Atlas          
        database. The pie chart sums flow by Norwegian zone for the selected
        year. The line chart shows incoming and outgoing flow between NO_4 and
        SE_1 for the selected months in the most recent year of available data.
        """
        )
